tasks.short: Warn other screeners not to open baggage suspected of containing explosives.

steps.what: Identify the baggage and decide the immediate no-open warning
Inform nearby screeners that the identified baggage must not be opened
Confirm colleagues understood the baggage identity and restriction
Write and check the brief warning event entry
Commit the checked warning entry to the checkpoint incident log

tasks.design: Keep the immediate warning and closed-loop acknowledgement human over {TELEPHONY}. Review the checkpoint incident-log form in {OTHER}, but its short new-fact entry and direct save remain manual; no assistant or administrative approval queue delays the warning.
tasks.previous_blocker: The warning depends on immediate context and reliable colleague acknowledgement.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is assumed to shorten this narrow safety communication.
tasks.still_hard: Correctly identify the item and ensure the right people heard the restriction.
tasks.human_edge: Communicate urgency clearly and notice a missed acknowledgement.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the screener's week or authority for this task.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: an immediate safety warning needs human confirmation; a log form does not establish that colleagues heard it.

assumptions: Boundary includes warning, acknowledgement and its short existing event entry; assessment of the suspected device and specialist response are separate. Shares are provisional, not an incident-time measurement.

s1 selects location, baggage_reference and restriction from observed facts under the local checkpoint protocol. s4 manually records those values, time and recipients_acknowledged after the warning. No structured-data feed is assumed.
s1 is the screener's immediate professional decision before the spoken warning, not an added supervisor permission step. s4 checks the final event entry before the separate direct human commit in s5.

Native forms and standard warning phrases are considered; they do not shorten the observation, acknowledgement or new-fact capture assumed here. There is no repeated report or separate send hidden inside the log entry.

Zero incremental upkeep because the existing radio and incident form are unchanged. US agency terminology in the task is mapped to the actual European checkpoint protocol without assuming US law applies.
unknowns: Whether the existing log requires additional duplicated fields
research_questions: Does observation reveal a separate duplicate incident report that should be assessed independently?

incremental.description: No new workflow or tool maintained

approvals.approved_version: s1 chosen current baggage identity, location and no-open restriction
s4 checked warning entry and checkpoint incident destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Both direct voice warning and the existing short event form retain all time. A template cannot supply new observations or acknowledgement, and no extra reporting baseline is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ask passengers to remove applicable items before passing through screening equipment.

steps.what: Ask passengers to remove required shoes and metal items
Remove required items and place them for screening
Check readiness and explain any remaining required action
Handle accessibility, medical or comprehension exceptions

tasks.design: First improve the existing checkpoint's approved static pictogram panels and instruction wording so routine passengers need a shorter spoken prompt. The screener still addresses each passenger, checks readiness and handles exceptions; no individual profiling, automated passenger decision or new passenger entry task is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: A long repeated verbal instruction is harder to follow across language and accessibility differences.
tasks.enabler_now: Approved pictograms and a shorter standard spoken prompt can convey routine preparation before personal clarification.
tasks.still_hard: Medical exemptions and passengers who cannot use the panels still need full individual help.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion or discomfort and give respectful, accessible instructions.

ambition.what: Provide routine divestment instructions usable by passengers who do not read the checkpoint's main language.

tasks.altitude: Less repetition of standard wording; the screener retains every readiness and exception decision.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: well-tested pictogram instructions can shorten repeated spoken explanations; the proposed labour benefit needs checkpoint measurement.

assumptions: Boundary is the divestment interaction, not security detection or document checks. Focal baseline is 80 and passenger physical effort is 20; passenger time remains unchanged.

Provisional s1 saving reflects a shorter spoken prompt using visible approved panels, not elimination of passenger contact. Central 70% remaining must be checked by observation; staff still address every passenger.

No structured individual inputs, recording, report or database write is part of this ordinary instruction task. Current divestment rules come from the checkpoint authority and are never inferred from the O*NET US wording.

Native existing signage and wording are tested first. One-time authority approval of the final panel and prompt precedes installation and is included in rollout/access. No per-passenger automated publication or send is added.

Static panels contain only current approved actions and accessible illustrations; no assumption is made that shoes must always be removed under every European protocol. Readers unable to use the panels receive the complete personal explanation.
unknowns: Current instruction length and panel quality
Applicable local divestment and exemption rules
research_questions: Does the shorter prompt preserve correct preparation and avoid increasing exception handling?

incremental.description: Check that the panel and prompt still match the current checkpoint rule
Approve and maintain accessible translations and pictograms

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 40*30%=12 focal-share hours: 12/80*100 minus 0.5 = 14.5%. Low shortens the prompt only 10%: 4/80*100 minus 0.5 = 4.5%. Passenger removal, readiness checks and exceptions stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Challenge suspicious people and verify badges and authorised business.

steps.what: Challenge the person and request their badge and reason for being there
Inspect badge authenticity and compare it with the holder
Look up badge validity and permitted zones in the access-control system
Judge the explanation and take the required access or escalation action
Write and check the challenge incident entry
Commit the accepted entry to the checkpoint incident log

tasks.design: Test a badge-reader shortcut to the current permissions view in the access-control system in {OTHER}, reducing identifier rekeying while preserving the screener's reading and judgement. The screener still challenges the person, checks badge authenticity and writes the actual incident outcome; only the checked log entry gets a separate controlled commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Badge verification can require manual identifier entry and navigation to a separate permission screen.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reader integration can open the exact current permission record.
tasks.still_hard: Valid credentials do not establish a legitimate purpose, and cloned badges remain possible.
tasks.human_edge: Assess the person's explanation calmly and notice mismatches with the badge or situation.
tasks.altitude: Less identifier entry; challenge and escalation decisions remain human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native badge-reader integration can remove identifier rekeying without deciding whether a person has legitimate business.

assumptions: Boundary is challenge, credential lookup and its incident entry; credential issuance and security response are separate. Provisional lookup benefit requires observed rekeying/navigation, not an invented search for a posted list.

Access administration produces badge_id, valid_from, valid_until, permitted_zones and revocation_status. s3 captures the presented badge through a reader and still inspects the returned fields; unreadable or unavailable records use the full manual lookup and local protocol.
The 50% s3 remaining covers reading, reader use and fallback; physical comparison in s2 is unchanged. No automated suspicion score, biometric identification or access grant is added.

s5 manually captures time, location, badge_reference, stated_purpose and challenge_outcome, checking the final payload before s6. Changes revoke a1. If native lookup and commit are already direct, remove their proposed saving.
Native configuration precedes code; reader permissions and employee consultation where applicable are included in access/rollout.
unknowns: Existing reader shortcuts and current lookup effort
research_questions: Does a reader-opened view clearly show revocations and zone restrictions without a stale-cache result?

incremental.description: Check reader-to-record links and permission-view freshness

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked challenge entry and checkpoint incident destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 15*50%=7.5 lookup hours and 3 commit hours minus 0.5 upkeep = 10. Low saves only 20% of lookup effort and keeps commit manual: 3 minus 0.5 = 2.5. No saving from the challenge or access judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Patrol work areas and identify suspicious items.

steps.what: Patrol the assigned work areas and observe objects and surroundings
Assess an observed item and decide whether to report a concern
Notify the control room of the observed concern
Write and check the patrol observation entry
Save the checked entry in the checkpoint patrol log

tasks.design: Keep patrol and concern assessment human, with direct control-room communication over {TELEPHONY}. Evaluate the existing patrol log form in {OTHER}, but retain its brief new-fact entry and direct save; a route dashboard or generated narrative does not replace seeing and assessing the actual area.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patrol value comes from physical observation and situational judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: No evidenced change is assumed to shorten this particular patrol task.
tasks.still_hard: An unusual item requires contextual assessment and a reliable response route.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a change in the environment and act on uncertainty appropriately.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in patrol time or decision rights.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a patrol log cannot replace direct observation; unrelated retail camera capabilities do not establish a saving for airport patrols.

assumptions: Boundary includes physical patrol, a concern notification when needed, and the existing short patrol entry. Shares are provisional across patrol rounds; notification and concern effort are averaged, not imposed on every no-concern round.

The screener produces location, observation_time, factual_description and action_taken in s4. A no-concern round records its actual route/time only; no nonexistent acknowledgement is required. Missing observations are never filled by a model.

Current patrol protocol comes from the checkpoint authority. Native patrol forms are considered before code; the assumed short current form has no duplicate narrative report or rekeying step to eliminate.
s2 chooses the current concern facts before the direct s3 notification. s4 checks its completed entry before the separate human save s5. Neither is a new supervisory approval delay.

Zero incremental upkeep because existing tools and procedures are unchanged. If the actual organisation copies patrol entries elsewhere, split and reassess that work rather than declaring it outside the boundary.
unknowns: Whether patrol records are already entered once
Actual patrol and incident workflow boundary
research_questions: Does observation reveal duplicated patrol paperwork that an existing native form can remove?

incremental.description: No new patrol technology or data mapping introduced

approvals.approved_version: s2 current observed concern, location and control-room notification scope
s4 checked patrol entry and patrol log destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Physical observation, judgement, direct notification, fresh fact entry and the existing direct save retain full effort; no new upkeep or assumed duplicated paperwork.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Protect immediate safety interactions while testing simpler instructions and exact credential lookup where those touch actual work.
role.ambitious_version: A screener who spends less time repeating standard wording while keeping observation, challenge and urgent warnings human.
